questions.question: You want to prevent direct pushes to the protected branch 'main' and allow only members of the 'developers' team to push. Which branch protection setting should you use?
questions.expected_answer: B) Use 'Restrict who can push to matching branches' and add the 'developers' team
questions.user_answer: A) Enable 'Require pull request reviews before merging' for the branch
questions.followup_question: Can you explain your reasoning for choosing option A over option B?
questions.feedback: Candidate chose A (require PR reviews) and then admitted uncertainty. The correct setting is B: use “Restrict who can push to matching branches” and add the developers team — that explicitly blocks direct pushes by everyone else. Requiring PR reviews prevents unreviewed merges but does not restrict which users or teams may push to the branch.

questions.question: You are rebasing the feature branch onto main and encountered a conflict in app.txt shown below. Fix the conflict by keeping the feature changes but produce a single clean final file (no conflict markers). Then list the exact git commands you would run to finish the rebase.
questions.expected_answer:
Final app.txt content:

Welcome to Project Alpha!
We use version 1.3 and new API.

Commands to finish the rebase:

git add app.txt
git rebase --continue

(If other conflicts appear, repeat resolution, git add <file>, then git rebase --continue until the rebase completes.)
questions.followup_question: Please provide the final app.txt content after resolving the conflict (the cleaned file with no conflict markers).
questions.followup_answer:
Welcome to Project Alpha!
We use version 1.3 and new API.
questions.feedback: Resolved file content is correct and the exact commands (git add app.txt; git rebase --continue) are provided. Did not mention repeating the resolve → git add → git rebase --continue loop if more conflicts occur.
